meaningful_now: Both artifacts contain a single rectangle-like visual target backed by a deterministic manifest and hashes.
The Excel oracle capture proves the live MSForms fixture displayed a 320x240 top-level window with a #2070C0 label fill region at x=41..166, y=64..125.
The current OxForms W002 counterpart proves the smoke PAL can render one FillRect into a 4x3 RGBA framebuffer and report a stable hash.
The artifacts can be linked by paths, hashes, commands, and rough rectangle-region observations.
not_meaningful_yet: A pixel diff between the Excel screenshot and W002 framebuffer is not justified because they use different surfaces, dimensions, colors, units, chrome, and control semantics.
The Excel label is an MSForms control inside a themed UserForm window; W002 is a PAL FillRect smoke command, not an OxForms UserForm or Label implementation.
The observed point-to-pixel relationship is not a calibrated Twips/points-to-pixels rule.
comparison.current_relationship: Calibration only: the Excel oracle supplies a measured target shape and metadata for future renderer work, while W002 supplies the current minimal OxForms rectangle output.
